### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 56 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **23** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a6cf988eb3afc4cbe23fac4caf71206943806c23` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3064633de8ec4f30a4b8542da063cb3e77cd90aa` — the merge of head `0ad415bbcc4163a7c5d2af4f9061427be9af3e9c` into base `a6cf988eb3afc4cbe23fac4caf71206943806c23`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3064633de8ec4f30a4b8542da063cb3e77cd90aa && git checkout 3064633de8ec4f30a4b8542da063cb3e77cd90aa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a6cf988eb3afc4cbe23fac4caf71206943806c23 0ad415bbcc4163a7c5d2af4f9061427be9af3e9c && git checkout -B drift-repro a6cf988eb3afc4cbe23fac4caf71206943806c23 && git merge --no-ff 0ad415bbcc4163a7c5d2af4f9061427be9af3e9c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a6cf988eb3afc4cbe23fac4caf71206943806c23
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `0ad415bbcc4163a7c5d2af4f9061427be9af3e9c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: brief 6973847132; card #34651 (body and all 4 comments: triage 6938946687, regrade 6969710529, claim 6972612725, os-dev-report 6973807530); parent #33187's dev report 6938771548 (open questions 1, 2 and 4) and ruling A 6915677641; PR #35162 (body and comments); the full diff against merge-base `3446f234f3` (16 files, +133/−3: 2 commits); the changeset; follow-up card #35164; and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at `origin/main` only.

Face: the committed file list touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path. `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` decides no face from the paths and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `yes (widening)`. So this is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, with no ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **CI on this head is still running.** 50 check-runs: 13 success, 16 skipped, 21 in progress, 0 failure. Still running: `Build Core`, `Test Core` (10 shards), `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Live E2E UI` and six `Lint ·` lanes (among them `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, which carries the NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, and `Lint · docs & code guards`). Complete and green: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`. I judge on what is complete. The seat must see the 21 in-progress runs finish green on this head before landing.
- **The `add-sso-user` door answer: widened, right.** `runAddSsoUser` adds one spread, `...(outcome.alreadyPending ? { pendingAgain: true } : {})`, beside the existing keys. The key is present only on a re-add of a pending person and is never `false`. The `alreadyPending: outcome.alreadyPending` line is untouched, so it is still on every answer with the same value. The status codes (`200` on a re-add, `201` on a fresh add), the `positions` / `permissionSets` / `notApplied` / `organizationId` / manager / `host` members and every refusal path are unchanged. The door pin asserts both halves: an email-only re-add answers `200` with `pendingAgain` `true` and `alreadyPending` `true`; the CONTROL fresh add answers `201` with no `pendingAgain` property and `alreadyPending` `false`. A re-add of a deactivated pending person also answers `pendingAgain: true`. That is correct, because the person is pending, and the dialog's `host.reason` row already says the invitation was not sent.
- **The `sys_user.add_sso_user` result dialog: one field added, right.** `{ path: 'pendingAgain', label: 'Already pending', format: 'json' }` goes in between `email` and `notApplied`. At `origin/main`, `ActionResultDialog.tsx:123` filters with `field.path === '' || value !== undefined`, and `readPath` returns `undefined` for a missing member. So the row is drawn only on a re-add, and a fresh add draws no `false` row. That is exactly what ruling A 6915677641 requires: it turned down "a misleading `false` row on every fresh add". `format: 'json'` fits a boolean (`valueFitsFormat` gives `json` any value, and `text` only a string). The import table's own `alreadyPending` column draws the same way. The sys_user pin checks that exactly one field reads `pendingAgain`, with its label and format, and its CONTROL checks that no field reads `alreadyPending`. The rewritten comment above `fields` is accurate: `notApplied` comes from `notAppliedOn`, which lists positions, permission sets and manager only.
- **Translation bundles: right.** Each of the 11 platform-objects bundles (en plus ten locales) gains one leaf, `resultDialog.fields.pendingAgain`, under `add_sso_user`. That is the same key route the sibling fields use. Each locale's value is the "already pending" half of its existing `alreadyPending` / `summary.alreadyPending` string, for example zh-CN `已在待激活中` from `已在待激活中，已再次通知`. No existing key is changed or removed. The dev ran `check-i18n-bundles --filter=platform-objects` locally with exit 0. CI's lint lane is still running (above).
- **Built entries: nothing removed, renamed or narrowed.** `@objectstack/plugin-auth`'s `.` entry re-exports `pending-sso-users.js` in full (`index.ts:102`). `runAddSsoUser` keeps its signature and its `EndpointResult` return type. The answer body is untyped, and no exported interface describes it (`ImportSsoUserRowResult` is the import row and is unchanged). No SDK method builds this URL (`auth-route-ledger.ts:263`: server-only). `@objectstack/platform-objects` ships `SysUser` with one more element in an existing array of the existing field shape, plus one more bundle leaf. Neither changes a type. No input a host, author or API caller could pass before is refused now.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The new key is computed from `outcome.alreadyPending`, which the door already held. The new alignment test stages the import door through its existing HTTP path.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/34651-add-user-already-pending.md`: right.** It bumps `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` at `patch`. Those are exactly the two published packages the diff moves; the tests are not published. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 says that `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and that a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. CI `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right.** It is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, and the arm is from the closed pair. An answer key present only when true, added beside an unchanged key, is a widening. The claim 6972612725 declared `Clause-②: yes` from the start.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No spec key, accepted value or metadata type is added. The `sys_user` change uses the existing `resultDialog.fields` row and the existing `json` format.
- **Changeset prose, checked against the diff: right.**
  - "answers `pendingAgain: true` on a re-add of a person who is still pending, and leaves the key out on a fresh add. It never answers `false`": matches the spread and both door pins.
  - "`alreadyPending` is unchanged and is still on every answer": the line is untouched.
  - "including when you sent only an email": the door pin is the email-only re-add.
  - "The dialog skips a field whose path is absent from the answer, so the row is drawn only on a re-add": true at `ActionResultDialog.tsx:123`.
- **The released 18.5.0 sentence (PR body claim): right for the clause the card names.** `packages/platform-objects/CHANGELOG.md` line 464 says "The Add User result names an address that was already pending". Before this PR, that was untrue for an email-only re-add, because nothing in the answer marked it and `notApplied` is absent when no column is sent. After this PR, the "Already pending" row is drawn on every re-add, so the clause is true. That meets the card's last Done-when bullet. The parenthetical that follows it is N2.

Findings:

- **N1 (nit): the door's prose descriptions do not name the new key.** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx:1340` ("answers `201`, or `200` with `alreadyPending`") and the route-ledger note at `auth-route-ledger.ts:263` describe the answer without `pendingAgain`. Both are still true, and the PR's Acceptance notes record the doc line. For now the changeset is the only place an API reader learns the key. Prose only, with no correctness or contract effect.
- **N2 (nit): part of the released sentence stays untrue in one rare case.** The 18.5.0 sentence goes on: "(the hosting organisation is told again, …)". For a deactivated pending person, no invitation is sent (`host.reason` reads `deactivated`). The Add User dialog itself shows this correctly, through its "Invitation not sent" row. Only the released CHANGELOG parenthetical is wrong, and it is the same class as follow-up #35164. Prose only: a released history entry.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- Parent open question 1 (6938771548, option B, "for example pendingAgain: true"): implemented as option B. The key name follows the cited precedent, the claim records that naming is the seat's call, and the card lists `pendingAgain` among its dedupe words. Parent open question 2 (option B: the released sentence becomes true once the fix lands): answered in ②. Parent open question 4 (the real-answer alignment pin): delivered as the `[#34651] the import result table reads members of a real row answer` describe. It stages a fresh add with an unknown manager, a malformed address and a re-add that sends a column, so every member the column paths name is answered on some row. Ablation A3 turns it red.
- NOT-MEASURED gate `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, needs a whole-workspace build): answered. It was declared as a narrowing, and CI `Lint · repo & tooling gates` carries it on this head. That run is still in progress, so the seat's green-CI check before landing covers it.
- Deviation, shared clone deepened (`--deepen=1500` for overlap-check, and a depth-1 fetch of `621a4876` for the teardown self-test fixture): process only, no contract effect. Accepted.
- Deviation, the relay forced `draft: true` on PR creation: process only. Accepted.
- Deviation, the label is "Already pending", not "Already pending, told again": answered and right. A deactivated pending re-add also answers `pendingAgain`, and no invitation is sent then, so "told again" would be false on that row.
- Deviation, translations hand-written into the generated bundles: answered. The generator's merge mode keeps them, and the dev ran `check-i18n-bundles` with exit 0. CI's lint lanes re-check it.
- Deviation, commit trailers are the model-free pair: process only.
- Out-of-scope finding, the import table's "Already pending, told again" label on a deactivated pending row: escalated, filed as #35164 (p3, `domain:server`, `pm:queue`).
- Out-of-scope note, `authentication.mdx:1340`: not filed by the dev. Recorded here as N1.
- The test that reads `SysUser` through `@objectstack/platform-objects/identity` resolves that package's `dist/`. `@objectstack/platform-objects` is a `workspace:*` dependency of plugin-auth at `origin/main`, and the existing `declaredAction` helper and import already use this route. CI's `Build Core` / `Test Core` (in progress) answer it.
- Process notes: the PR is a draft. Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay), assignee `os-warren`, so no extra author note is owed. The two findings are nits, so this is the final round unless the head moves for a reason other than prose.
